summary: Do not move to Ready yet: A5 can clear tool-derived provenance across exchanges before filtering removes the remaining taint evidence. B3 also needs an explicit owner disposition as a proposed exception to the no-tool-details scope. This was a static design review, not an implementation test run.

findings.title: Do not reset assistant provenance at an exchange boundary
findings.body: A5 marks a concluding assistant message false whenever its own exchange has no tool output and its source geometry is complete. A normal counterexample is: exchange b0 reads external content and reports it; in b1 the user asks for a shorter restatement, which the assistant supplies without another tool call. The restatement still derives from the external content, but the specified mechanical rule gives it false. The filter can then keep b1 and drop b0, leaving the consolidation model only explicitly false provenance and no source evidence of the earlier tool origin. This conflicts with the same row's requirement to retain tool-derived claims as attributed reports. The existing ordinary Tier-3 gate (src/core/dream/validate.js:198-214) checks the submitted provenance flag, whereas B2's independently derived invocation-window taint applies only to skill learnings, so it does not repair this path. The inference is that a candidate supported by this restatement can now be treated as trusted when its external origin has been removed.
findings.recommendation: Specify conservative propagation of assistant taint through later exchanges that can reuse prior tool-derived context, computed before selection. For this iteration, marking subsequent assistant conclusions untrusted after observed tool output or uncertain source context is a simple bounded option; verified primary user messages can remain false. Add a synthetic cross-exchange restatement case where filtering drops the first exchange and confirm the retained reply remains true. No tool text or evidence store is needed.

routed_scope_objections.title: B3 proposes a tool-detail exception that needs an explicit owner choice
routed_scope_objections.body: B3 (line 188) permits model-visible originally observed skill names and error state. The scope record excludes tool-call details and tool-result content and its final unresolved item 4 expressly says not to add tool details back to model input to hide a compatibility problem. In the existing Claude parser, the skill name comes from tool_use.input.skill and the error state from the paired tool_result.is_error. These are compact structured tool details, even though they contain no free-form result text. They are useful for the existing dream skill's learning discovery rules (SKILL.md:214-234), but they are not required to preserve code-owned authorization: B2 can supply the validator independently. Ask the owner to accept this narrow metadata exception explicitly, or omit it from model input and have learning discovery use retained primary dialogue while B2 continues to validate claimed invocations. This scope choice is routed rather than counted as a verdict finding; the current maintainer-feedback checklist does not name this exception.
